datasets.title: MovieLens 100K
datasets.description: The GroupLens movie catalog across three primitives - movie JSON, KV aggregates, and similarity-ready genre vectors.

includes.detail: One document per movie (movie:<id>) with title, year, genres, and rating summary stats.
Collection movie-genres - 19-dimension cosine vectors, so nearest-neighbor queries work right after clone.
Catalog aggregates under meta: - movie count, genre list, source id.
The sample branch trims the catalog to the ten most-rated movies - the small/full split without duplicating storage.

datasets.title: Agent Memory, With Experiments
datasets.description: A synthetic agent's memory - episodes, event trace, working state - pre-forked into three retention-policy branches.

includes.detail: Episodic memories (memory:episodic:<n>) plus live working state under state: - working memory, task queue, profile.
An append-only observation / tool_call / reflection trace with hash-chained sequence integrity.
Run metadata under meta: - seed, step count, policy notes.
Three retention policies forked from one baseline; the raw event log is identical on every branch.

datasets.title: Titanic Passengers
datasets.description: Passenger records from the 1912 voyage, with raw and cleaned branches so curation is a branch switch away.

includes.detail: One document per passenger (passenger:<id>) with class, fare, embarkation, survival, and cabin fields.
Aggregates under meta: - survival rate, passenger counts.
raw keeps the nulls; cleaned imputes them, with every curation step preserved as document history.

datasets.title: Stack Overflow Q&A
datasets.description: 1,500 Python-ecosystem posts as JSON documents with comment threads embedded - one get returns a full discussion.

includes.detail: Questions and answers keyed post:<id>, with their comment threads inline - no join against a comments table.
Per-tag post counts under meta:tag:.

datasets.title: GitHub Events
datasets.description: 2,000 developer-activity events across ten open-source repos, as append-only streams grouped by event type.

includes.detail: PushEvent, PullRequestEvent, IssuesEvent and more, in arrival order - the natural shape for what-happened-when questions.
Per-type event counts under meta:count:.

datasets.title: Wikipedia Articles
datasets.description: 200 article records over ten topics - one JSON document per article, with a KV title-to-slug index on top.

includes.detail: One document per article (article:<slug>) with title, categories, internal links, and word counts.
An exact-title index (title:<Title> → slug) plus catalog totals under meta:.

datasets.title: A/B Test Results
datasets.description: One experiment, three arms, each arm on its own branch - the cross-branch comparison workflow as a dataset.

includes.detail: One document per session (session:<n>), plus a per-arm summary:metrics document.
The experiment definition under meta: - hypothesis, arm sizes.
control, variant-a, and variant-b forked from the shared definition - the same query per branch is the whole analysis.

datasets.title: Strata Benchmark Results
datasets.description: Thirty real runs from Strata's own performance suite, replayed as an event log instead of a flat CSV.

includes.detail: latency, scaling, and workload suite runs in order - two months of the engine's own numbers.
One full result document per run (run:<id>).
Latest-run pointers under meta:latest:.

datasets.title: Iris Flowers
datasets.description: Fisher's 1936 measurements, with the dataset's real documented corrections preserved as document history.

includes.detail: One document per flower (iris:<row>) with the four measurements and species - corrections visible via json history.
Per-species counts under meta:.

datasets.title: ISO Reference Codes
datasets.description: Country, currency, and language codes from three ISO standards - the lookup table agents shouldn't bundle by hand.

includes.detail: Direct lookups - country:US, currency:JPY, language:fr - with catalog totals under meta:.
A detail document per entry across all three code tables (249 countries, 178 currencies, 184 languages).
